title: What Would Make Us Stop?
scene: You are about to start a project. Before investing more time, you decide what evidence would make you stop or change direction.
sceneJa: プロジェクトへさらに時間を投入する前に、どんな結果なら中止・方向転換するかを先に決め、結果を見た後で基準を動かさないようにする場面。

chunks.en: Before we invest more time in the project,
chunks.ja: プロジェクトにさらに時間を投入する前に
合意しておくべきです
何が起きたら中止するのかについて

chunks.en: we may keep changing our explanation
chunks.ja: 説明を変え続けてしまうかもしれません
私たちの考えに反する

chunks.en: Setting a clear threshold in advance
chunks.ja: 明確な基準値をあらかじめ設定しておくことで
結果を公平に判断することが

chunks.en: If the test falls below that threshold,
chunks.ja: もしテスト結果がその基準を下回ったら
計画を再検討するべきです
それを擁護するのではなく

questions.question: Which chunk boundary is most natural?
options: we should agree on / what would make us stop
we should / agree on what / would make us / stop
we should agree / on what would / make us stop
questions.explanation: ‘Agree on’ stays together, followed by the content of the agreement: ‘what would make us stop’.

questions.question: What does ‘the evidence goes against us’ mean here?
options: The evidence conflicts with our view.
questions.explanation: ‘Go against’ means to conflict with or count against an idea, expectation, or position.

questions.question: Why set a threshold in advance?
options: To make the test more complicated.
To reduce the temptation to change the standard after seeing the result.
questions.explanation: A pre-set threshold helps keep the judgment consistent even when the result is disappointing.

speak: Sound firm, but not pessimistic. Land clearly on ‘what would make us stop’. In the final sentence, contrast ‘reconsider the plan’ with ‘rather than defend it’.
review: Previous session: ‘what we will do with the result’, ‘move on to testing’, and ‘what we do next’. Today adds an exit condition: decide in advance what result would make you stop or reconsider the plan.
